pr_title: DRAFT: Add YAML tags for controlling variable merge behavior
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY

This adds a few YAML tags for controlling how variables are merged when there are duplicate names across multiple sources.

There are 2 commits in the PR. The first commit adds a `!merge` tag, and is for controlling merge behavior of maps/hashes/dictionaries/whatever_you_want_to_call_them. The second commit adds `!append` and `!prepend` for controlling merging of lists/arrays. This is a bit more complex of a change, as Ansible sometimes will merge the same variables multiple times, resulting in a list being (pre/ap)pended multiple times. Maps don't have this issue as it'll just result in a key overwrite with the same value. So for lists we have to track where the list came from to prevent duplicate entries.  
Note that the merge behaviors are not automatically recursive. The tag must be applied at each level to merge that level (otherwise it replaces).

This is definitely a draft, as there are things I would probably clean up and re-arrange. However with the code as it is, it makes it clearer what's going on. There also would need to be tests, addressing the linter, etc. Right now it's just up so it can be reviewed conceptually before proceeding.

I've tested this with group_vars, host_vars, playbook vars, block vars, task vars, & role vars.

Closes #83903 

While `DEFAULT_HASH_BEHAVIOUR` is also deprecated-but-not-quite, and has a messy history (#72021, #72669, #73089, #73328, #74215), this change will hopefully provide an actionable replacement for the functionality, and allow it to truly be deprecated.

```

```

```

  - debug: var=foo
    vars:
      foo: !merge
        six: six
      blockvar: blockvar
  vars:

      seven: seven
    taskvar: taskvar
```

##### Review
A few questions that need answering:
* Should maps & lists functionality be separate? Meaning should this PR focus on map merges only, and list merges be a separate future change? Maybe use suffixes for lists, like `!merge:append`.
* What should things be named? Should the merge tag names be something else?

> https://yaml.org/type/merge.html

I'm not sure what you're getting at. I don't see any relation to that, and this change. They're completely different. This change is about merging variables of the same name across sources (multiple yaml documents consumed independently by python code). That functionality you linked is about merging multiple nodes of different names within the same document.

YAML tags aren't really the best mechanism for this- the existing Ansible usages are arguably an abuse of what was supposed to be a type hint for deserializers and schema validators. They're not usable as a parallel data plane (ala XML attributes)- you only get one per node, so if you need another one (eg, to override a problematic YAML implicit resolver like bool or octal int, or to signal more than one custom behavior), you're hosed. They also cause a lot of load/interop problems with other tooling. We're stuck with `!vault` and `!unsafe` for the foreseeable future, but we'll likely never add any more.

The oft-deferred data tagging mechanism (now slated for 2.19) supports a fully composable tagging scheme that serves as that additional metadata plane, and we've already successfully prototyped a per-var dynamic replacement for `hash_behaviour: merge` that allows for variable-level opt-in merge behavior like this (in a way that doesn't break the world for portable content like existing HB:M does).

We definitely haven't forgotten- I was probably the loudest voice inside the core team for "we need to keep HB:M until we've got a suitable replacement" (much as I detest its current impl), and we're on the cusp of being able to do it "correctly"...

issue_context.title: yaml tags for controlling variable merge behavior
issue_context.body:
### Summary

I've worked in several ansible shops, and every one of them has had issues with structured data in group_vars. The naive approach is for people to put structured data in group vars (structured, meaning arrays, dictionaries, etc. anything other than single scalar values), especially structures several layers deep. The obvious problem with this is that it's not conducive to overriding. If you put `foo: { bar: baz, pop: tart }` in `all.yaml`, you can't override just `foo.bar` inside another group_vars file without also overriding `foo.pop`. There are several options to combat this:

1. Flatten everything - Instead of the above, you would have `foo_bar: baz, foo_pop: tart`. This gets very repetitive, and doesn't really work for arrays, or anything which is iterated over rather than accessed via absolute reference (full name).
2. Redefine the entire nested structure when overriding any element - This is problematic as the inability to override a single node make it difficult to evolve the data, or have multiple sources which may override.
3. Set `hash_behavior = merge` in the config. This option is deprecated, for obvious reasons in that it has a high likely hood of breaking 3rd party collections and whatnot which don't expect the behavior.

I think it's apparent that we need the ability to merge data from multiple sources, but we also need to be able control that behavior. I think the only place that makes sense to control the behavior is on the source of the data. Meaning where the override value is defined, in that same place is where the merge behavior is defined.

For this, I think that YAML tags would be an appropriate solution. Therefor the proposal is to add a set of YAML tags which control the merge behavior on variable conflicts. The tags would apply to a single element of a dictionary (map), and not be inherited recursively. The default behavior would remain as is, to replace the value of the same key.

The names of the tags are immaterial at this point, but I propose 3 tags & behaviors to go with:
1. `!merge` - This tag, when specified on a dictionary (map) element, would result in the contents of the dictionary being merged with the existing dictionary of the same key. Elements in the new dictionary which are not in the existing dictionary would be added. Elements which already do exist (same key) would replace the existing value, unless that element also has a YAML merge tag, in which case the tag specification is observed for nested element.
2. `!append` - This tag, when specified on a list, would result in the new list being appended to the existing list of the same key.
3. `!prepend` - This tag, when specified on a list, would result in the new list being prepended to the existing list of the same key.

For all the above tags, the type of the value being merged from & into must be the same. Meaning merging a dictionary into a string makes no sense, and an error should be produced.

----

Note that I looked into adding this as a custom vars plugin, however it's not possible. The problem is that the the plugin receives a call to `get_vars()` for every group individually, and does not have access to the existing variables, so it cannot merge them.

Therefore, support for this has to be added to ansible itself. Ansible already [adds several tags of its own](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/e3ccdaaa2ef27b1de6db9e37b523677a605d5a5e/lib/ansible/parsing/yaml/constructor.py#L148-L178), and also [adds its own contextual data to loaded variables](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/e3ccdaaa2ef27b1de6db9e37b523677a605d5a5e/lib/ansible/parsing/yaml/constructor.py#L46). So the idea would be to define new YAML constructors which add a "merge_behavior" attribute to the loaded variable. Then when [`combine_vars()`](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/e3ccdaaa2ef27b1de6db9e37b523677a605d5a5e/lib/ansible/utils/vars.py#L79) is called, it would check for the property which defines the behavior, and merge accordingly.

----

Example, for a host with group `foo`:

```
# group_vars/all
users:
  bob:
    id: 123
    groups: [ staff ]
  marcy:
    id: 456
    groups: [ admin ]
```
```
# group_vars/foo
users: !merge
  thomas:
    id: 789
  bob: !merge
    groups: !append
      - admin
  marcy: !merge
    groups: [ staff ]
```
```
# Effective result:
users:
  bob:
    id: 123
    groups: [ staff, admin ]
  marcy:
    id: 456
    groups: [ staff ]
  thomas:
    id: 789
```

Hi!

Thanks very much for your submission to Ansible.  It means a lot to us that you've taken time to contribute.

Unfortunately, we're not sure if we want this feature in the program, and I don't want this to seem confrontational.
Our reasons for this are:

* This is not something we plan on implementing or have the capacity to do so
* The datatagging feature being worked on today may enable us to implement this feature but even then it would still require a lot of work to do so

However, we're absolutely always up for discussion.
Because this project is very active, we're unlikely to see comments made on closed tickets and we lock them after some time.
If you or anyone else has any further questions, please let us know by using any of the communication methods listed in the page below:

* <https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/community/communication.html>

In the future, sometimes starting a discussion on the development list prior to implementing
a feature can make getting things included a little easier, but it's not always necessary.

Thank you once again for this and your interest in Ansible!
